title: Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage — Working Out the Card Payment on a Resident Coinsurance Charge
content:
**Applied charge.** A card payment the resident or representative makes during the call is applied to the resident's original coinsurance charge for the coverage's latest booked coinsurance block, that is, among the coverage's booked-days entries in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 the one whose last service date is the latest, and it settles the resident's share of the days that charge prices less the payments already applied to that charge.

**Record test.** The card payment is worked out only for a paid block that passes this record test: its service month carries one booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100; at most one such entry of the coverage has the last benefit day just before the paid block's first benefit day; the bed-hold records book at most one leave for its service month and take back none of that leave's held days; its booked-days entry carries at most one day reversal for each reason and none for a booking error; no hospital-day or leave-of-absence reversal on it covers a held night of that leave, and each such reversal counts every day of its span; an uncertified-day reversal on it counts every day of its span except the held nights and the hospital-day and leave-of-absence days inside the span; and, when the supplemental effective date falls after the paid block's first service date, the block before it either has a resident charge billing exactly 100, 50 or 25 percent of that charge's own days times its own daily rate, to within half a percentage point, or carries a secondary charge and no resident charge; and, when the resident's charge for the paid block stands, its day count equals the paid block's booked days less the days of every day reversal posted against its booked-days entry on or before the date that charge was posted; and the paid block's last service date falls in 2024 or later. The block before the paid block is the coverage's booked-days entry in the band of benefit days 21 through 100 whose last benefit day is the day before the paid block's first benefit day; its resident charge is the resident coinsurance charge posted for it that is not a rebill of a denied secondary share.

For a block that passes its record test, the resident coinsurance charge, the card payment, the rate-year correction, the reduction for reversed covered days and the bank draft each count the days before the supplemental effective date as their own policies state, and only for such a block; for every other block, the tier that sets the split is the one in effect on the days of service: a Medigap policy changes the split from the carrier's policy effective date and QMB protection from the first day of the month after the state's QMB determination, so days before the supplemental effective date keep the earlier split, and none of these five figures is priced for it.

### The amount, clause by clause (Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage)

(a) The card payment prices each day it counts at the daily coinsurance rate of 217.00, and days before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share of 100 percent.

(b) The supplemental effective date the card payment reads is the one recorded on the coverage; a coverage that records none has the tier on file in effect on every day of the paid block.

(c) The card payment counts the paid block's covered days, which are its booked days less every day reversed against its booked-days entry, once the resident's charge for the paid block stands, and no day before it stands; the rounded figure less the payments already applied to that charge, net of any returned payments, is the card payment, never less than nothing and never more than the card payment maximum of 5000.00.

(d) The days the card payment counts before the supplemental effective date are first its calendar days of the paid block before that date: when the date falls after the paid block's first service date and on or before its last, the days from the first service date up to the day before the date; when it falls after the last service date, every calendar day of the paid block; otherwise none.

(e) Each kind of day named below that is not a covered day is taken off those days, never leaving fewer than none nor more than the days the card payment counts.

(f) A day reversed as a leave-of-absence day is not a covered day: when the paid block's booked-days entry carries a leave-of-absence reversal, its reversed days inside the paid block come off the days the card payment counts before the supplemental effective date, all of them when its last reversed day falls before that date, those from its first reversed day up to the day before the date when the date falls after its first reversed day and on or before its last, and none otherwise; without such a reversal, none come off.

(g) Days the card payment counts before the supplemental effective date take the earlier share; every other day it counts takes the resident share of the tier on file. The resident share of the tier on file is that tier's resident share percent in the cost-sharing split schedule. When the tier on file prohibits balance billing, as the QMB Medicaid Crossover tier does, the card payment bills the resident nothing for any day on or after the tier's supplemental effective date, those days taking the tier's resident share of nothing, while days before that date keep the earlier split, QMB protection not reaching back before it.

(h) The card payment adds, over the days it counts, the daily rate times the share each day takes, divides the sum by 100 and rounds it half up to the cent once.

(i) A card payment worked out above the resident's charge's open balance, which is its amount less the payments and adjustments posted against it plus any returned payments, shows that the charge was billed below what its days call for; the card payment is then not taken under this policy, and any payment the payer sends is applied only up to that open balance, the remainder being returned.

### Hypothetical worked examples

*Example 1.* A paid block in the Medigap Plan A or B tier (resident share 100 percent) runs from the 19th to the 26th of a month, 8 booked days, no reversals, and the coverage records no supplemental effective date. The resident's charge for the block stands, and 236.00 has been applied to it with nothing returned.
- 217.00 times 8 times 100 is 173600; divided by 100 and rounded once: 1736.00.
- Less net payments of 236.00: 1500.00, which is not less than nothing and not more than 5000.00.
- The charge's open balance is 1500.00, so the card payment is **1500.00**.

*Example 2.* Same block, but the charge was billed at 1650.00, so its open balance after the 236.00 payment is 1414.00. The worked figure of 1500.00 is above 1414.00, so the card payment is not taken under this policy; a payment sent is applied only up to 1414.00 and the remainder is returned.

*Example 3.* A worked figure of 6120.40 is taken as 5000.00, the card payment maximum.
